entry.title: EP43 【意外總比明天早到：用平常心扛住裁員與股市大跌！ 】2026年11月20日
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @Sophie06344746（婷的后花园☀️❤️🏝️） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

大家好，這裡是 CLEC James 漫談，我是 James。今天應該是第43 期了。我們有幾個事情來談一下，那最後當然談一下最近市場在下跌。

一、面對裁員風險與現金流的重要性

第一個就是最近，也不是最近啦，就是時不時就是有人會被裁員。所以假設你是剛畢業上班、裁員，當然就是繼續找工作，那這個應該不是問題，有什麼工作都可以做，只要有薪水進來，扣除開銷之後有一點錢可以投資，那這個人生就是會非常富有。

那有些中年了，已經中年了，那被裁員有些人會緊張。那其實如果你是 40 幾歲，也工作了將近 20 年了，理論上做好投資的話，假設一開始畢業就做好投資的話，你應該會有一些資金。那只要能夠有 15 倍年開銷，除了在中國以外，在其他地區能夠直接投資QQQI 的，有 15 倍年開銷應該就可以放輕鬆了。放輕鬆就算要退休也可以，不然就是找一個輕鬆一點、收入低一點的工作，一樣可以快樂生活、富足。

所以像今天有一個朋友他就被裁員嘛。一開始他有點震驚，覺得他是一個工程師，那在公司是這麼重要的工作，竟然也可以被裁員。這個就是「意外總比明天早到」了，所以大家一定要有風險意識。

那還好就是這個朋友他已經有 15 倍的年開銷了，所以他可以做QQQI，生活費就沒問題了。還有他想說要另外找工作呢，還是接受一個派遣工，派遣工就是約聘的吧。其實也不用再找工作了，就做一個約聘的工作，有工作做就好了，那如果要找工作再說吧。其實他已經可以做半退休的狀態了。

所以我們的工作不能保證我們一生，可是我們的投資理財卻可以護我們一世。所以還是要做好投資理財、風險控管。所以平常投資理財，做好現金流管理，留好緊急備用金，什麼工作都可以做，有現金流、有薪水進來就好。

二、單筆買進還是分批買進？克服市場心理誤區

還是有人認為、還是有人擔心，就是說：「啊，我賣完房子拿到錢了，我應該要單筆買進還是分批啦？」當然就是單筆買進就好了啦！你要分批當然你還蠻折磨自己的啦。那有的人也會說：「老師，現在市場在下跌，你還叫人家單筆對嗎？」

誰知道明天會漲會跌啊？如果我會說分批，那跟整個統計的概率就不符合嘛，對不對？所以我們人會在一個趨勢裡面，認為這個趨勢會持續下去。所以在上漲的時候就會認為市場不會跌，在下跌的過程就認為市場不會漲，那這就是人的一種誤區了。

所以市場漲多了就是會跌，市場跌多了就是會漲。這個是巴菲特所談的「貪婪與恐懼」。那當然你也不知道人類的貪婪會到什麼地步，你也不知道人類的恐懼會到什麼地步，所以無法猜高低點。那既然都什麼都不知道，當然就是立即市價買進。

那你如果覺得單筆立即市價買進你很痛苦，真的是很恐怖——其實一點都不恐怖啦——不過你如果要分批，就分三個月內買完就好了。因為你現在買，市場已經下跌幾十 percent 了嘛，你現在買QQQ 620、630 塊，總比人家買 750 的來得便宜了嘛！所以你已經接到了黃金雨了，所以單筆買進應該高興，而不是緊張或恐懼。

三、市場下跌的真相：融資斷頭與風險控管

在股票市場下跌是很正常的。可是當市場在飆漲的時候，很多人都過度樂觀。我一直跟大家講要做好準備、做好緊急備用金，不要過度、不要融資。像現在這個下跌的狀況，你會看到就是開盤就跳空下跌 2%，那現在可能跌到 3%——指數喔，指數——那其他個股都6%。我看很多個股都已經從高點下來腰斬了。

雖然今年來講，有些個股到目前為止還漲了一兩倍，可是從高點下來已經腰斬了。那這個一定有很多人是被套在這個山區的啦。那你如果是實股拿著也就算了，問題是融資的人就是會被強迫賣出。所以如果一開盤就跌 2%、3%，那這個都是券商一開盤就因為你沒辦法補足保證金，券商就會直接市價賣出，所以會有這種開盤就跳空的事件發生。

那你像昨天開高走低，這個就是融資還沒有全部出來，今天應該是融資就開始出來了。所以等到融資斷頭都結束之後，那過去這一群人過度樂觀的都離開市場之後，該賣的都賣光了，市場就會止跌，就會開始再往上了。這就是重複不斷，每次市場就是這樣子：樂觀、追高、市場下跌、恐懼、補倉、繼續跌、再補倉、再繼續跌，最後斷頭、這些人都抬出去了，那就沒事了。

所以我一直跟大家講，就是市場跌 80%，你還能正常吃飯睡覺，這個才是投資的準則。「六尺高的人淹死在平均五尺深的水」，就是仗著說我六尺，那平均的水只有五尺，所以我應該可以走得過去。其實平均五尺不代表永遠五尺啊，對不對？就是可能它有很深的 18 尺深的海溝。

所以就算說我們說年化報酬 10%、20%、15%，對不對？可是你不能仗著每年都是這樣子啊，它有一年可能會跌 80% 啊。那你如果是融資的話，或過度槓桿的人，那你就會吃到苦頭。雖然未來很美好，可是你可能會見不到陽光。所以大家一定要謹記在心：風險控管。

四、認識自己與投資哲學

認識風險、理解風險、控制風險，這是所有投資第一課。如果你不知道風險，那你就一定在風險之中。

所以很多人不認為需要留現金，很多人認為這個要追熱門股，或者是追更會漲的個股，或者是類股等等等等。沒有錯，可是一定要知道就是市場有很大的波動。我們投資 QQQ 的波動當然就會高過SPY 嘛，那你其他的個股、類股的波動一定高過 QQQ 嘛。像QQQ 現在下跌十幾 percent，可是有的個股、類股都腰斬了。

不是說那些投資標的錯誤，所有的投資標的跟投資方式都是中性的，沒有好壞。好壞因人而異。當你買進一直漲、一直漲，你就認為它好；那如果跌，你就變成不好。如何讓這個好跟不好都不存在，這個就是投資的哲學。

所以巴菲特說過：「別人貪婪時恐懼，別人恐懼時貪婪。」那現在大家進入了恐懼時間，那你應該做什麼事？那以後要記得，當別人貪婪的時候、市場一直飆漲的時候，你就不要過度槓桿；當別人恐懼的時候，那你應該要做什麼事？絕對不能賣出喔，就是一定要抱緊。

市場短期是投票機啦，現在市場的下跌誰也沒辦法決定，因為這個只能決定於那些融資、槓桿的人都被平倉之後，這市場才會結束。所以會被賣出的人、被強迫賣出的人賣完之後，這市場就會落底了。

五、歷史經驗與面對市場波動的態度

其實像巴菲特長期回報這麼高的，他過去波克夏的股價也有三次下跌將近 50% 了。在 1973 年到 1975 年的時候，他跌 59%；1998 年到 2000 年，他跌掉 49%；2008 年到 09 年，他也跌掉51%。像在 1987 **年股災，**25 天內就跌掉 37%。所以我一直跟大家講風險，而且留足現金流。這個是等到你碰到了，你才知道我在講什麼。

所以股市長期會有非常優渥的回報，可是短期它是翻臉無情，所以你要能夠接受這個短期下跌的震盪。

所以很多人如果現在你開始有 panic**（恐慌），或者是你開始睡不著覺了，那代表：第一個，你可能已經不適合投資了；不然就是你的部位太大了，你的現金不足。那如果你是現金不足造成你的這種緊張、恐懼，那以後記得，那你就要多留現金，安全重要。**

可是有些人不是，也投入不多，就投入了 20% 資金，一下跌他也緊張得跟人家好像全倉的人緊張一樣的恐懼。那這樣子的人，其實你要了解你自己，你可能就不適合投資了。所以這個每個人要先了解自己之後，才進來市場。那當然我們鼓勵你們大家都要勇於投資了，可是有些事情真的就是強求不來。

巴菲特的公司都跌過這麼多次，那市場下跌的次數可能更多嘛，而且深度也會更深嘛。所以這個就是好像天氣春夏秋冬，冬天一定會來，那跟大家講要棉襖準備好，可是你如果不準備棉襖，你冬天就比較難熬嘛。所以這個就是一個經驗，如果你這次沒做好，那下次就做好一點嘛；那如果你這次比較辛苦，那下次可能就習慣了、就知道了。

所以理論上如果市場下跌，是對於沒準備好的人是一種折磨，可是對於準備好的人是天上掉下來的禮物。至於市場下跌是你的禮物還是一種災難，其實都不是現在決定的，而是過去你的資產配置跟心理素質決定的。

六、不回答個股問題與結語

好，這裡就是有些朋友來信，那就問：「啊，我個股要賣嗎？這個等到回本再賣嗎？那我有其他的投資，理專建議我這個可以買嗎？」這個你都不要問我，你手上有什麼股票我一點都不關心，我也不會給你建議，我們只建議納斯達克 100 指數基金。

那會問這個問題的，就是說：「哎，可不可以買這個？可不可以買那個？」或者是說：「我手上的個股要不要拋掉？我現在個股或我的基金已經虧那麼多了，是現在賣掉還是等到回本再賣？」這個都不是我會回答的啦。這個你去看我們影片，看完 300 部影片之後你還找不到答案，那你可以來問我，我再跟你講繼續看影片。

沒辦法，這種事情——個股、類股，不是納斯達克 100 指數基金的，我都不評論啦。不是它不好，是我叫你賣也不對，不叫你賣也不對。所以這個東西當你事情發生之後，你再來問我就太晚了。

市場在大漲的時候，就沒有人來問我要不要把這些賣掉。那市場這個漲三倍、五倍的時候，就嘲笑我買指數太慢了，個股比較快，或者是什麼比較快。當然是啊，那個買也沒錯啦，只是說這個市場無常嘛，你能夠飆得多快、飆得多高，你就可能跌得多深，這個就是Beta**（貝他值）嘛，就是波動率嘛。你既然能夠快速的飆漲，那一定會快速的下跌，這個就是自然現象嘛。這個自然現象就是對稱嘛，所有事情都是對稱的，所以這個都是要學習的啦。**

好，所以總歸市場下跌是天上掉下來的禮物，不要隨便賣股票，你看戲就好，不要演戲。那等市場落底、自然落底之後，它就會上漲，這就是市場本來的自然現象，春夏秋冬嘛。那現在市場進入了冬天，那冬天過了春天就來了，所以投資者永遠樂觀、永遠迎向陽光。

**好，大家好好吃飯、好好睡覺、好好跟家人相處，市場不要理會就好了。**OK，好，就這樣。這個就像好像感冒嘛，得到感冒你能做什麼，對不對？頂多就是讓自己舒服一點就好了嘛。一樣，市場下跌你就想辦法讓自己舒服一點，吃得好、睡得好、沒煩惱，市場就會過去的。

我們 40 幾年來這種事情已經碰過很多次了，一年兩次的話也 80 幾次了，所以對我來講是家常便飯，可是對你們來講可能是第一餐飯。好好吃、好好享受這個市場下跌的禮物，那未來你就會更了解市場、更淡定。

OK，好，今天我們的 James 漫談就談到這裡，謝謝大家，拜拜。

entry.title: We have a Slopware Factory
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @sentry（Sentry） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

I write a lot about Junior - our (open-source) internal robotic Slack-enabled intern. I will also tell you that it’s as much of a Software Slopware Factory as anything is. Its name is on more commits than any other single contributor at the company. It’s definitionally a state of the art software factory, but I bet it doesn’t behave like you think.

What even is a Software Factory?

It depends on who you’re talking to, and if the conversation is today, last week, or next week. I can tell you what it means today - what it means to have a state of the art factory. I find it easiest to reason about a real-world workflow.

My world revolves around Slack

Most of my conversations with Junior are pretty simplistic like the above (which is a real conversation from a few hours ago). I give it a pretty straightforward task, without much detail, and I expect it to fill in the remainder. Sometimes it does it well, sometimes it produces utter garbage. It’s kind of odd given it’s a factory, you’d expect the production lines to have some consistency, but they do not.

In this case the ask is pretty straightforward. I have an experiment, in Junior, for a kanban board visual of work. It turned out to be junk, so I’m deleting it. You’ll note I gave it no context - no repository, no details on where it’s at or what it encompasses. Its job is to figure it out. It’s my intern. I give it an assignment, and I expect it to come back to me if there was something it couldn’t resolve on its own.

A lot of times it will figure this out via memory, and if that fails, it will do it through a variety of tools at its disposal. I frankly don’t care how it fills in the blanks, as long as it does it efficiently and correctly (although efficiency here leaves a lot to be desired). In this case, it searched some past conversations to fill in the context, as we can see in the web UI for the transcript:

We landed this feature a few days back, it figures that out, and it realizes I simply want the experiment removed from the codebase. So it does the work, and comes back to Slack with a Pull Request ready to burn my eyes with:

The Pull Request in this case is good. It’s got a simple clear description, the code changes look correct (or at least they have convinced me as much - I obviously don’t know as I didn’t write the code).

I give it a quick glance on the code changes - seems to reflect the PR description. Low risk, I don’t spend a lot of brain power on it. I’m sure it fucked something up I’ll figure out later, but in this case it probably just failed to find every last reference to the Kanban experiment. Maybe I’ll be pleasantly surprised, either way, Schrödinger’s Cat. I click Approve, satisfying my requirements for this service of self-review or peer-review (which is minimally allowed at Sentry). Might as well let it auto merge while I’m here - CI will probably flush out any bugs. I’m sure the agent didn’t delete any of my regression tests. It would never do that.

It proceeds to decide I need to be updated in Slack, so it updates me, and a few minutes later it merges it.

If there were any failures in the CI, I was not made aware of them, as Junior automatically determined if it should address them, as well as any PR feedback I might have left - of which, I left none, because I barely looked at the code.

After a combined total of $1.32, and five minutes of my time, the Kanban board is gone.

That is a software factory - at least as of this week. It enabled me to take an intention, whether I had clarity or not, and act on it with minimal effort. Its main benefit was taking away some of the tedium of doing this. I didn’t open Claude Code, I didn’t have to instruct it to monitor CI, I didn’t have to think. In this case that was fine, but they’re not all like this, and this is the state of the art (at least for a company with real-world customers and liabilities).

If you made it this far, you’re probably wondering why you found no insights. Why were there no crazy next generation automations? Why was the system not building itself?! Because that is all a myth. Our system has memory - that doesn’t make it self-improving. Our system can act on your requests - that doesn’t make it automated. Our system is here to help you be more efficient at your job, to help you take an idea and execute on it. That is the state of the art.

It will not replace us, it will simply allow us to be more productive.

entry.title: Your agent is now a link: introducing Agent Share & Import
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @MOJOAI_HQ（MOJO） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

You built an agent that works. It watches the price you care about, it acts the way you want, and it keeps a record of every step. Then a friend asks, “how did you set that up?”, and the only way to answer was a screenshot and a long message.

Today that changes. With Agent Share & Import, a MOJO Agent can travel as a single link. Anyone who opens it can read the full plan, have it checked against their own account, and start it themselves. Nothing runs until they press start, and it only ever uses their own money.

Key takeaways

  • Share any agent from its card or its run details. You get a plan poster, a ready-to-paste share text and a link.
  • Hide the amounts with one tap if you’d rather not show your sizing.
  • Whoever opens the link sees the full execution plan before anything else.
  • When a signed-in user opens it, MOJO checks the plan against their account first: available funds, amount, and anything that can’t carry over.
  • If the numbers don’t fit, they can lower the amount or have MOJO draft their own version of the agent.

How to share an agent

  1. Find the agent. Open Assets in the sidebar. In the Agent section, every agent has a share icon next to its status.
  2. Check the card. Tap the share icon and the Share panel opens. On the left is a card for the agent: its name, its result so far (return, principal, how many trade actions it took and its status) and your invite code with a QR code.
  3. Decide on amounts. The Amounts toggle at the top hides the figures, on the card and in the message, so you can share the idea without your sizing.
  4. Send it. Use Save image for the card, Share to social to post it, or Copy message for a ready-to-paste text. The link icon at the top copies just the link. The message reads like this:

At the top of the panel, MOJO says plainly what a share means: anyone who opens it can view the full plan and, once conditions are met, start it with their own account.

The card shows what one agent did in one account over one period. It’s a record, not a promise about the next run.

What happens when someone opens your link

If they aren’t signed in, they land on a public page with the agent’s name, who shared it, what it’s for, a summary and the full execution plan, step by step. Below it, they can sign in or register.

If they’re signed in, MOJO opens the agent straight into its approval page, marked as shared by you, and runs a pre-check against their account:

  • How much they have available on the venue the agent trades on.
  • Whether the amount in the plan fits.
  • Whether any step depends on something that can’t move from your account to theirs.

They can read the summary and the execution plan, edit the agent, or start it. Starting is always their own decision, made with their own funds. Your money, positions and open orders never move.

📷

When the numbers don’t fit

Good plans get shared to people with very different balances. MOJO handles the mismatch instead of leaving the reader to guess:

  • A one-time trade (for example, open one position at market): lower the amount on the approval page. MOJO re-checks it, and if it fits, the agent can start.
  • A repeating or conditional agent (for example, a price check every 10 minutes): you can choose to edit it into your own version. MOJO pre-fills the request, reads the shared plan and your balance, and drafts a new agent sized to what you have. The draft still credits the original sharer.
  • A plan that can’t carry over: some agents rely on things only the sharer has, like a specific open order or existing holdings. MOJO says exactly that, for example: “The plan takes over holdings that already exist in the sharer’s account, so it can’t be started with your account as is.”

Paste links into chat and compare

Share links also work inside a conversation. Paste one into the chat box and MOJO opens it next to your draft, which stays where it was. Paste two, add “compare these two plans”, and MOJO reads both and lines them up for your account. The comparison covers the trigger, the size, the leverage, the worst-case loss, and whether each one can run with what you have right now.

entry.title: -$6 Trillion In 45 Days: Is This A "Bubble" Or An Opportunity?
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @Sophie06344746（婷的后花园☀️❤️🏝️） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

Our most common question right now: Is there an “AI bubble” and did it pop? US stocks have now lost an average of -$225 billion per day, for 31-straight trading days. Below, we provide a comprehensive breakdown of how we got here, what is happening, and what we see next.

Since November 2022, we have been highly bullish on AI, calling it the biggest technological revolution in history. Our view of “own assets or be left behind” was built on the combination of innovation-driven returns and compounding inflation.

Over the last 6 weeks, the AI trade has faced one of its biggest tests since inception, among the likes of April 2025 amid the trade war. **Bookmark this Article **and refer to it over the coming weeks.

The reality is that AI is disrupting the status quo of the global market, economy, and civilization. Disruption yields polarity in sentiment, and swings in asset prices only exacerbate that polarity.

That is exactly what we are seeing right now.

The Last 45 Days Have Been Chaotic:

Before we begin, it is important to understand just how much has happened since October 6th, the last time the S&P 500 hit a record high.

Over the last 45 days, the market has seen countless Iran War headlines, Q3 2026 earnings season, concerns around AI CapEx and Free Cash Flow, the October Fed meeting, US Midterm Elections, the Nvidia, $NVDA, controversy, and ultimately a loss of -$6 trillion in market cap.

On top of this, Anthropic’s IPO just raised over $100 billion in the biggest IPO in history, which has been a clear strain on market liquidity over the last few sessions.

As an investor in times like these, it is important to step back and ask yourself one key question: What has changed and what is priced in?

A Lot Is Priced-In: CapEx and FCF Concerns:

The selloff began primarily over concerns about Capital Expenditures on AI by large cap technology companies in the US and the implications on Free Cash Flow and profitability looking into 2027 and 2028.

These are real concerns.

The combined CapEx of Amazon, $AMZN, Alphabet, $GOOGL, Meta, $META, and Microsoft, $MSFT, rose +$36.9 billion in Q3 2026, to a record $201.9 billion.

This figure has more than doubled over the last 12 months and is up +356% since Q1 2024. Big Tech has now spent $1.6 trillion on CapEx over the last 3 years.

However, it is also important to acknowledge that record infrastructure spending is a necessary condition for the biggest technological revolution in history. A brief period of negative free cash flow is the short-term cost of a long-term buildout.

A lot of these fears are already priced-in, but they will persist until more clarity on the ROI of this CapEx is obtained - likely into Q1/Q2 2027.

There has never been a market with so much fear yet so much growth. S&P 500 companies have reported +31.9% YoY EPS growth so far in Q3 2026, the strongest YoY growth rate in at least 4 years.

Actual earnings have beaten estimates for 13 consecutive quarters, the AI buildout is stronger than most people realize.

Democrats “Sweep” US Midterms - The “Trump Put” Ends:

Next, we believe the catalyst behind a major portion of the recent drawdown in technology stocks is related to the outcome of the US Midterm Elections which effectively ended what we are calling the “Trump Put.”

As seen in President Trump’s first term from 2016 through 2020 as well as Trump’s second term to date, markets objectively find comfort in times of volatility when President Trump has the ability to sway them. The “Trump Put” is a hedge, a notion that if the market gets ugly, President Trump will intervene because stable markets have been a top priority for him.

With the Democrats’ “sweep” of the Midterm Elections, we believe the “Trump Put” has effectively come to an end. Further catalyzing the end of this backstop was the below post on November 4th:

President Trump’s ability to intervene in markets has been partially eroded by the change in control of the US Senate and US House. Calls for an AI ban have gained traction and markets have priced in aggressive regulation and potential bans on AI when Democrats take control in January 2027.

While the end of the “Trump Put” will not be reversed and will spur sharper drawdowns in US equities, we believe regulation concerns are overdone.

The US banning AI will not happen. Such a ban, if even possible to enforce, would effectively mean the US surrendering its position in the global AI race to China.

There will be more regulation and likely new taxes, but the market is assuming a more extreme case than what we believe will come to fruition.

Ultimately, the US should want to win, regardless of who is in power.

The Fed Is Hiking Into An Anxious Market:

On top of the concerns surrounding AI investment and the shift in the political landscape, the Fed is hiking interest rates aggressively.

As the Iran War nears its 300th day and US inflation has been above the Fed’s 2% target for 67-straight months, Fed Chair Warsh has made it clear that his top priority is to lower inflation to 2% with no exceptions.

This means the already expensive burden of building AI is getting even more expensive. Not to mention, the US Federal debt situation is even worse.

As shown above, US investment-grade corporate bond sales are expected to rise +$37 billion YoY in November, or +27%, to $175 billion, the highest for any November on record. We believe the Fed’s rate hikes into this backdrop have further contributed to the recent instability. Can this change?

The shift in political power and the recent market downturn has led to a ~22% drop in oil prices this month. Couple this with the market’s instability and the Fed’s outlook into 2027 will likely change, especially if it is clear that the Iran War is closer to its end.

On November 2nd, we published the below analysis on US oil prices heading into the US Midterms, calling for a drop below $93.00. Since then, prices have hit their lowest since August 2026. On Sunday, we will publish the latest edition of The Kobeissi Letter, consider subscribing to gain access here.

Even with the drop in oil prices, “higher for longer” will remain for now, but we believe the possibility of less restrictive Fed policy into mid-2027 is growing.

Nvidia, AMD, And The China-Chip Situation:

Over the last two weeks, Nvidia has lost Jensen Huang, the leader of the AI Revolution, its stock is down -40% in a matter of weeks, AMD is now being accused of smuggling chips into China, and markets have priced in major concerns around the implications.

As you have all likely seen, we have been very vocal on the Nvidia situation, taking an early stance that Jensen Huang is innocent until proven guilty. We called for the board to leave the door open for Jensen until a definitive independent investigation establishes the facts.

We took this view because of how innovative and impactful Jensen Huang has been for the AI Revolution and for the success of the United States. Nvidia’s stock price now reflects a near-certainty that Jensen Huang will not return and has effectively written off the company’s forward guidance entirely.

The same is happening with AMD after a short seller report on November 19th accused the company of smuggling chips into China, a claim that has been far from substantiated.

As a result of these events, the Forward P/E of the tech sector has collapsed to its lowest since March 2020.

Nvidia’s Forward P/E is down to 9x, making it one of the cheapest stocks in the S&P 500, and by far the cheapest relative to the growth in earnings that the company is seeing.

What does this mean? The market does not believe the “E” portion of the Forward P/E. Despite Nvidia guiding ~$750 billion in revenue for FY2028, even without Jensen Huang, the market refuses to believe it.

There is a ton of room for surprise baked into this market right now.

Sentiment Is At Crisis Levels Right Now:

On October 15th, we published our analysis titled the “Stealth Bear Market” which identified a bear market underneath the surface of the S&P 500, particularly in technology stocks. This marked the beginning of the shift in sentiment. It did not begin with the Midterm Elections or the Nvidia situation.

As shown below, those events only accelerated the shift in sentiment.

The Volatility Index, $VIX, is now up over +100% from its October low and posted its biggest daily gain since February 2018 on November 5th. Now, couple this sudden surge in fear with the Anthropic, $ANT, IPO which significantly reduced liquidity in the market.

Institutional demand for the IPO hit $400 billion, with retail orders at $100 billion after the books closed Tuesday, nearly 8x the initial $64.4 billion raise at the $78 share price expected at the time.

The combination of a sudden shift in sentiment and a large drawdown in liquidity led to the price action we saw this week, with everything trading lower from stocks, to gold, to crypto, and more.

Hedge funds posted their largest trailing 6-week net outflow in over a decade this month. It was simply a dash for the exit.

Once liquidity returns, we believe the market will stabilize.

In Conclusion: What Comes Next?

This brings us back to our original question: Is there an “AI bubble” and did it pop?

Our answer is no.

There is no question that the AI Revolution is facing one of its most significant tests to date. However, we believe the market has begun pricing in a far more pessimistic outcome than what the underlying fundamentals currently suggest.

We believe the market is in the midst of a normal correction. Even if the S&P 500 fell an additional 10% from current levels, we would still be within the range of a healthy correction.

To call for a prolonged bear market well into 2027 is betting that the above factors will not only play out, but worsen. There is a lot of negative sentiment already accounted for in current asset valuations, we would be cautious about calls for a 30%+ drop in the S&P 500 which are quickly spreading.

The reality is that sentiment has become extremely polarized and we believe this polarization will create an opportunity, as it always does.

At current levels, the market is pricing in a combination of sustained higher interest rates, aggressive AI regulation, disappointing returns on AI infrastructure investment, and prolonged uncertainty around some of the most important companies in the technology sector. There is a lot of room for positive surprise heading into 2027.

We are not suggesting that the market has necessarily reached its bottom. Volatility will remain elevated, liquidity remains constrained, and further downside is entirely possible as uncertainty persists.

However, the risk-reward setup is becoming increasingly attractive, particularly in high-quality technology companies with strong balance sheets, accelerating earnings growth, and durable competitive advantages.

We believe a significant amount of bearishness is already priced in, while the market is overlooking the potential for positive surprises. Once the dust settles, we expect dip buyers to rotate back into high-quality technology stocks quickly, similar to April 2025.

Asset owners will continue to win in the long run.

More about our strategy: Remain objective and following a process during times of disruption are key to being a successful investor.

An objective and systematic approach is what has led to our outperformance of market benchmarks.

As shown below, our investment strategy has returned nearly five times the S&P 500 since 2020.

entry.title: 搭建 AI 时代的 e2e 测试实战教程
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @leo_xiaolei（刘老板） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

端到端（E2E）测试一直是研发链路里最贵、最脆弱的一层：写起来慢，改个按钮文案就大面积报错，挂了还得人肉翻截图和日志。大模型普及之后，大家自然想把这件事交给 AI，但真落地就会发现：**让 AI 全权接管测试，只会得到一套「贵、慢、飘、还会编造结论」的昂贵玩具。**这篇实战教程会带你从 0 到 1 搭一套能上生产环境的 AI E2E 测试体系。我们以开源的 Agent-Native 测试框架 e2e 为底座，用一个虚构的「订单管理后台」贯穿全篇，完整覆盖：框架选型与订阅接入、AI 随机探索测试、以需求为准的用例规范、零 Token 回放机制、反例故障注入、智能分诊与自动建单，以及 CI / Agent 集成。

一、先定核心原则：让 AI 干活，不让 AI 当裁判

在敲下第一行配置之前，必须先避开 AI 做 E2E 测试时最容易踩的四个坑：

  1. AI 会编造期望。 让大模型「读需求写测试」，它经常写出 PRD 里根本没提过的断言，甚至凭空捏造一段看似合理的需求原文。
  2. AI 操作不可复现。 同一个操作步骤，这次点对了按钮，下次可能走偏；用例时过时不过，团队很快就会对测试红灯彻底麻木。
  3. 每次都调模型太贵。 如果几十上百条用例每次跑 CI 都要让模型一步步看屏幕推理，一次构建就是几百次调用，耗时和账单都扛不住。
  4. AI 自己判对错不可信。 如果「功能算不算通过」也交给模型用视觉或自然语言拍板，那「测试裁判」本身就成了一个需要被测试的黑盒。

整套实战方案只围绕一句话展开：让 AI 干活，但不让 AI 当裁判。

在后面的搭建过程中，你可以随时对照这张职责边界图——脚本、框架与 AI、确定性规则、人，各自只干自己最擅长的事：

可以看到，AI 真正出手的环节被严格收敛在三处：辅助生成用例与随机探索、执行易变的页面操作、失败后的只读初步分诊。至于「期望对不对」「用例过不过」「是不是产品 Bug」「能不能转正」，全部交给确定性规则和人来拍板。

二、为什么选 e2e 框架：AI 时代的原生适配性

传统 E2E 框架（如 Playwright、Cypress）是为人手写脚本设计的，每个点击都绑定具体的 CSS/XPath 选择器，页面稍微重构就会大面积失效；而市面上另一批纯视觉/纯 Prompt 的 AI 测试工具，又往往绑定封闭云服务、按次收高额费用，且很难写出严谨的确定性断言。

这也是为什么我们在底座选型上推荐使用开源的 e2e 框架（TesterArmy/e2e，Apache-2.0 协议，TypeScript 栈，同时支持 Web 与移动端）。它不是在传统框架上硬套一个大模型外壳，而是从底层面向 AI 时代重新设计的 Agent-Native 测试框架，核心适配性体现在四个方面：

1. 混合编程范式：自然语言操作 + 确定性代码断言

在同一个 .e2e.ts 文件里，e2e 允许把「脆弱的交互路径」交给自然语言指令 agent.act(…)，把「严肃的结果判定」保留给类 Playwright 的确定性检查 expect(screen…)。前端改了按钮样式或位置，AI 靠语义依然找得到；但页面该显示什么数据、接口该返回什么值，仍然按代码精确核对。

实战取舍提醒：e2e 框架本身也提供语义断言 agent.assert(…)（用裁判模型看屏幕判断），方便快速原型验证。但在本文搭建的生产级体系中，我们刻意禁用 agent.assert() 作为通过标准，严格遵守「AI 只操作，规则判对错」。

2. 支持开发者订阅接入，不再被 API 账单和单一厂商绑架

AI 测试难以在中小团队推广，一个很现实的阻力是接入成本和账单管理。e2e 在模型接入层做了彻底解耦（Bring Your Own Subscription / Model）：

  • 直接复用已有订阅：开发者本地写用例、调试或做探索测试时，无需单独申请高价按量 API Key，可直接通过 OAuth 登录复用手头已有的订阅额度——例如 npx e2e login openai（ChatGPT Plus / Pro）、npx e2e login github-copilot（GitHub Copilot），以及 opencode-console、spacexai 等。
  • API Key 与网关兼容：团队级或服务器环境支持直接接入 OpenAI、Anthropic 等标准 API Key，也可对接 Vercel AI Gateway、OpenRouter 统一做路由和审计。
  • 离线 / 纯回放模式：CI 流水线跑回归时，甚至可以配置为不接入任何模型，纯走本地录像缓存。

3. 原生 AI 随机 / 探索性测试（Semantic Exploratory Testing）

传统自动化测试有一个天然盲区：它只能验证你提前想到的路径。 而传统的 Monkey 测试或随机点按工具又太「傻」，只会满屏幕乱点坐标，往往卡死在登录态、表单校验或无关弹窗里。

e2e 的 AI 探索模式（e2e explore）与语义级交互能力，把随机测试升级成了带业务理解的探索性测试：

  • AI 能读懂页面结构和控件语义，像真实用户一样在系统里自主漫游——尝试意想不到的菜单跳转、非常规的表单组合、边界输入和连续操作，专门用来挖掘「PRD 没写死、人也没想到，但用户一操作就会白屏或报 500」的深层 Bug。
  • 在实战定位上，AI 随机探索测试与需求回归测试形成互补：前者负责「发散式排雷」，后者负责「确定性守门」；探索过程中揪出来的典型故障路径，反过来又能沉淀为正式的回归用例。

4. 智能回放缓存（Replay Cache）与 Agent 生态友好

这是 AI E2E 能真正跑进每日 CI 的关键：第一次运行 agent.act(…) 时，模型现场观察页面并执行操作，框架会自动将这套底层操作序列与页面状态缓存在 .e2e/cache/ 中；后续再次运行时，直接按缓存确定性回放，零模型调用、毫秒级响应、结果完全一致。

同时，e2e 的 CLI 结构简洁，天然适配 Coding Agent（如 Claude Code、Codex 等）和 MCP 客户端调用，方便把测试直接嵌进 AI 辅助开发闭环。

三、实战第一步：初始化框架、接入订阅与跑通 AI 随机探索

1. 安装与初始化

准备 Node.js（建议 20+ / 22+）环境，在你的测试仓库中执行初始化向导：

交互式向导会引导你完成三项选择：

  1. 目标端：选择 Web（底层驱动如 Playwright）或移动端模拟器；
  2. 模型接入方式：选择已有订阅、API Key / Gateway，或暂不配置（纯回放）；
  3. 目录脚手架：自动生成 e2e.config.ts 和示例测试目录。

2. 按场景配置模型连接（订阅 vs CI）

场景 A：本地开发与调试 —— 复用个人订阅

完成浏览器 OAuth 授权后，本地即可零额外账单驱动 Agent 录制新用例和跑探索测试。

场景 B：统一配置 e2e.config.ts

在 e2e.config.ts 中显式声明被测地址、浏览器引擎、超时和回放缓存策略，避免把环境细节散落在各个测试文件里：

3. 先跑一次 AI 随机探索测试摸底

在正式批量写回归用例前，可以先对「订单管理后台」的测试实例放出一轮 AI 探索测试，检查页面有没有明显的死链、未捕获异常或表单崩溃：

跑完之后，把 AI 探索过程中踩出的真实页面异常整理成问题单，但不要直接把探索日志当成验收标准。接下来，我们进入严谨的「以需求为准」回归测试体系搭建。

四、实战第二步：建立「逐字可查」的需求清单

要彻底杜绝「AI 编造期望」，必须从源头切断自由发挥的空间：测试平台只认需求文档（PRD）的逐字原文。

1. 用结构化 YAML 摘录验收标准

不要手写需求总结，也不要从研发路线图的「完成条件」里拆需求（路线图里混着「文档合入」「代码重构」「内部门禁」等无法从外部验证的工程项）。正确的做法是：直接从 PRD 的功能验收标准里逐字摘录，每条绑定文档路径、章节锚点、逐字原文以及摘录时的 Git Commit：

2. 建立文档变更联动机制

在仓库里加一条检查脚本，每次同步 PRD 更新时，校验清单里每条需求的 quote 是否仍然存在于对应文档的最新版本中（只允许空白字符差异）：

  • 对得上：需求有效；
  • 对不上：说明 PRD 改了，所有关联该需求 ID 的用例自动标记为「可疑」，进入重审队列。

3. 避坑：覆盖率口径一定要诚实

很多团队做测试平台，最容易被「好看但虚高」的覆盖率骗过去。实战中务必从一开始定死三条口径：

  1. 只数本平台的正式用例：被测系统自己的单元测试、集成测试不能算进 E2E 平台的覆盖率，测试平台必须保持独立视角。
  2. 分母只算「已交付（delivered）」的需求：还没开发完的功能单独列出来，避免把「功能没做」和「测试漏写」混为一谈。
  3. 没有需求依据的用例宁可删掉：比如老用例里测了「列表每页 50 条」「必填项为空弹某句提示」，如果 PRD 里根本没写，就删掉等产品补齐文档再加——而不是让依据变成「我觉得应该这样」。

这样做短期内会让覆盖率数字大幅下降，但暴露出来的问题极其干净。比如 PRD 写着「导出记录需包含操作人与导出时间」，而后端接口只返回精简字段——用例报错后，谁都不用扯皮，这就是明确的需求与实现落差，直接交由产品和研发拍板改哪边。

五、实战第三步：编写生产级用例与数据准备层

有了需求清单，就可以写第一条符合生产标准的 e2e 用例了。

1. 标准用例写法：顶部溯源 + 操作即检查

看下面这条「按买家筛选订单并导出 CSV」的完整示例：

编写用例时，用 Lint 或入库前脚本强制锁死四条铁律：

  • 依据逐字核对：注释里 「」 括起来的依据，必须逐字出现在声明的 需求 原文里，多一个字、改一个词都直接拦下；
  • 页面源码只决定怎么操作，不决定期望：AI 写用例时可以读前端代码找按钮文案，但「点完该看到什么」只能从 quote 推出来；
  • 每个 act(…) 后必跟确定性 expect(…)：防止 AI 在某一步走偏后一路错下去，最后阴差阳错给个绿灯；
  • 禁止 sleep 固定等待，禁止用 agent.assert 判通过。

2. 数据准备层的两个真实深坑

每个测试文件头部声明自己需要的测试数据（买家、订单、商品），通过后端接口创建与清理，文件之间互不共享，天然支持高并发执行。在实现 prepare / cleanup 封装时，有两个坑建议一步到位规避：

  1. 清理逻辑必须扛得住乐观锁并发冲突 被测系统写接口通常会用带版本号的 If-Match 做乐观锁。并行跑完收尾删数据时，一旦撞上版本冲突直接抛错，环境里就会留下越来越多脏数据，最终污染其他用例。 做法：收尾脚本统一做成「先读取最新版本号 -> 再带版本执行写/删 -> 遇 412/409 冲突自动重试」。
  2. 在框架层统一处理 ETag / 版本号协议格式 HTTP 规范要求 If-Match 里的 ETag 值带双引号（如 “v42”）。有些被测服务早期版本校验宽松，不带引号也能过，升级后突然严格起来，会导致全量用例瞬间挂掉。这类纯协议细节必须在测试框架的请求客户端里统一封装，绝不能误报成产品缺陷。

六、实战第四步：跑通三种回放模式，避开「两位数字」深坑

1. 把 e2e 的三种运行方式对应到工程场景

配合 e2e 的回放缓存机制，我们在工程上明确切分出三种运行模式：

  • | 运行模式 | 执行行为 | 典型命令/参数示意 | 适用场景 |
  • |—|—|—|—|
  • | 只回放（Replay-only） | 严格按 .e2e/cache/ 回放，对不上直接判失败，绝不调模型 | 严格缓存模式（不回退 AI） | CI 门禁、每日定时回归。零模型成本、毫秒级 |
  • | 标准运行（Standard） | 有录像就回放；页面变了导致对不上时，自动切 AI 接手并重录缓存 | npx e2e run（默认） | 新用例首次录制、前端改版后的主动重录 |
  • | AI 现场操作（Live） | 绕过录像缓存，每一步都实时调用模型推理 | npx e2e run --no-cache | 探索新页面、验证 Prompt 与 Agent 鲁棒性 |

CI 绝对不能「自己修好自己」 很多人初用 AI 测试框架，会觉得「CI 里开着自动自愈多省心」。这是大忌：录像对不上说明页面结构或路由发生了变化，这件事必须被暴露出来让人确认，而不是被 AI 悄悄绕过去，掩盖掉真正的回归风险。

2. 建立「重录审计」规则

允许 AI 自动重录固然省力，但也埋着一个隐蔽风险：如果某次 PR 里既更新了 .e2e/cache/ 里的录像，又修改了 .e2e.ts 里的断言，Review 的人很难一眼发现「期望是不是被悄悄放宽了」。

硬性门禁：在 CI 里加一条 Git Diff 审计脚本——录像文件和断言代码禁止在同一个变更里同时修改；专门的重录分支只允许改动缓存录像文件。

3. 避坑实录：一个「两位数字」引发的 20% 随机失败

如果你上线回放后遇到「偶发的录像过期」，先别急着骂框架不稳定，先查一下你的测试数据 ID 是怎么生成的。

回放一个动作后，框架需要通过对比 URL 确认「是否跳到了录像里记录的页面」。但业务 URL 里经常带着动态 ID，例如 /orders/ord-mw4cl90k。回放框架为了容错，会把路径中「看起来像随机生成的 ID」替换成占位符再比对。常见的一条识别规则是：由字母和数字混合、达到一定长度，且至少包含两位数字。

如果你习惯用 36 进制时间戳 Date.now().toString(36) 拼接唯一后缀，灾难就来了：

  • 录制那次生成了 mw4cl90k（含 3 位数字），框架把它识别成动态 ID 占位符；
  • 某次回归生成了 mw4llqku（只含 1 位数字），框架把它当成了固定的路由词，和占位符对不上，直接报错「录像过期」！

算一笔账：36 进制中后 5 位全为字母的概率约为 (26/36)^5 ≈ 19.6%。这意味着大约每跑 5 次就有 1 次毫无征兆地失败；而且随着时间推移，时间戳前缀里偶尔变成纯字母时，失败率还会直接翻倍。

根治办法：

  1. 所有用于路由或实体的唯一测试后缀，统一改用纯十进制时间戳（全是数字，100% 被识别为 ID）；
  2. 给测试框架补一条单元测试：直接调用底层的路由比对函数，拿未来一整年的时间戳样本批量跑一遍，确保录制的地址和未来的动态地址全部匹配。以后谁不小心改回 36 进制，单测立刻拦截。

七、实战第五步：搭好生产级闭环（五关转正、反例验证、智能分诊与建单）

单条用例跑通只是完成了 30%，要让团队真正长期信任这套测试体系，还需要补齐四块工程基建。

1. 人在环里：一条用例从生成到转正过五关

不要让 AI 生成的用例直接进主干，建立清晰的五关漏斗：

  1. AI 生成初稿：选定需求 ID（或基于一段用户场景再反向绑定需求 ID），让 AI 读需求原文和页面源码，生成用例放进待审队列。
  2. 自动化硬闸（确定性检查）：脚本自动扫描——是否有分组、是否声明了需求 ID、依据是否逐字出自该需求且无夹带私货、每个 act 后是否紧跟检查、是否存在 sleep 或 AI 裁判断言。任何一条不过，直接打回，不进待审。
  3. 交叉 AI 评审（仅排序不拍板）：换另一个模型审查「期望是否严谨推出、断言会不会太弱」，产出评分只用来给待审队列排优先级，不具备通过权限。
  4. 稳健性检查：将待审用例打乱随机顺序，连续重复跑 5 次，必须 5/5 全过。
  5. 双屏人审：审核界面左边放 PRD 需求原文，右边放用例期望与断言，强制实行「作者不能审自己的」，转正时记录审核人。甚至可以偶尔往待审队列里混入几条故意改坏的「投毒用例」，用来统计人审团队的实际检出率。

2. 用「反例（故障注入）」证明用例不是摆设

覆盖率 90% 的测试集，依然可能抓不出任何 Bug——如果断言只写了「页面打开没白屏」，系统写库挂了它照样绿灯。

对核心高风险需求，要配反例（Counterexample）：故意往被测系统注入一处故障让需求被违背，跑一遍相关用例，用例必须失败才算合格；随后自动恢复环境，再重跑一遍确认恢复正常。

一次反例执行只有三种结果：抓到（Pass）、没抓到（断言太弱，退回重写）、出错（脚本/环境异常，无结论）。长期看，「反例检出率」是比代码或需求覆盖率诚实得多的质量指标。

反例会短暂破坏被测服务，务必安排在专用隔离实例上运行；且「故障恢复后的那次重跑」绝不能省，它用来证明环境已完全复原、用例本身没有假红。

3. 失败分诊流水线：聚类 -> 规则 -> 历史 -> AI 只读初判

线上大面积报错时，最消耗人力的是「20 条失败其实是同一个接口挂了，人却要翻 20 遍日志」。搭分诊模块按四步走：

  1. 先按根因聚类：提取 错误类别 + 失败步骤 + 归一化后的断言消息 + 相关接口 生成根因签名，签名一致的失败合并成一组，整组只做一次分诊。
  2. 规则能判的直接判：例如只回放模式下报路由/元素对不上，规则直接归类为「录像过期」，不花一分钱调模型。
  3. 复用历史人工结论：此前人已在分诊卡上确认过「判对了」或手动修正过的根因签名，下次再遇到直接沿用。
  4. 剩下的交给 AI 做只读初判：把证据目录（失败截图、DOM 结构、操作轨迹、测试数据核对结果、被测系统状态）喂给分诊 Agent，只开放读文件、搜索等只读工具，要求输出固定 Schema 的 JSON（归类、置信度、一句话结论、证据精确行号/路径、出错组件、建议下一步）。归类严格枚举为 7 种：产品缺陷、用例问题、测试数据、环境、录像过期、不稳定、不确定。
    **AI 的结论只是初判，必须由人点确认才算数。
    **

服务器部署踩坑提醒：分诊 Agent 在本机跑得好好的，上服务器却一直报「无权读取证据目录」——通常是因为证据目录在 Agent 工作目录之外，服务器沙箱权限更严。调用 Agent 时必须显式声明可读的证据路径范围，同时显式限制只读工具白名单，永远不要依赖运行环境的默认权限。

4. 自动建单与 Flaky 隔离

人确认是「产品缺陷」后，自动建单遵循五条机制：

  • 指纹去重：用「用例 + 失败步骤 + 错误类别 + 归一化断言 + 相关接口」算出指纹，写入工单隐藏注释；建单前先搜未关闭单，命中则只追加评论不重复建单。
  • 大面积熔断：单次运行失败超过阈值（数量 + 比例），大概率是测试环境挂了，熔断为只建一张「大面积失败」单。
  • 自动指派：按 需求交付人 -> 模块负责人 -> 兜底人 三级路由。
  • 自动闭环：修复后连续 3 次回归通过自动关单；关单后复发自动重开；关单若未关联回归用例则自动评论提醒补齐。
  • 全链路脱敏：证据和报告入库前统一脱敏，并配扫描脚本防止明文 Token / 密码泄露进工单。

Flaky（不稳定用例）隔离的修正规则： 同一个被测版本上，用例一过一挂就自动进入隔离清单（挂负责人与到期日，继续跑并记录数据，但不卡主流程，到期未修自动告警）。但注意一个极易误杀的边界：「录像过期」不要算作不稳定——只在回放模式稳定挂、切标准模式 AI 接手后通过，这叫「该重录」，不是 flaky；唯一的例外是「同一个版本上，该用例之前在只回放模式下明明通过过，这次突然回放失败」，这说明回放本身飘了，照样算 flaky。

八、实战第六步：接入 CI / Agent 生态与成本防线

一套现代测试平台的使用者不只是点网页的 QA，还包括 CI 流水线、夜间定时任务，以及未来帮开发验证改动是否破坏功能的上游 Coding Agent。为此需要暴露一套干净的远程调用接口：

1. 机器令牌与最小权限

  • 按调用方签发独立 Token：原文仅在签发时展示一次，数据库只存哈希；所有操作日志记录具体令牌名，出问题可精准溯源。
  • 严格隔离判断权：机器令牌允许触发运行、拉取结果、跑反例、提交 AI 生成的待审用例，但一律拒绝「替人拍板」的操作（用例转正、确认分诊归类、修改系统阈值、解除 Flaky 隔离）。

2. 为脚本和 Agent 设计的 CLI 协议

对外提供的命令行工具遵守三条 Unix / Agent 友好规范：

  • 平台忙碌时自动排队等待，不用调用方自己写死循环轮询；
  • 用明确的退出码表达结论：0 通过、1 有用例失败、2 平台或运行出错、3 超时；
  • 传入 –json 时，标准输出（stdout）只输出唯一一份结构化 JSON（包含失败分组与证据链接），进度日志全部写进标准错误（stderr），上游 Agent 拿到结果直接解析交给人看。

3. 三道成本防线

把大模型账单控制在几乎无感的水平，靠的不是换廉价弱模型，而是三道工程设计：

  1. 回放比例作为第一核心指标：日常回归坚持走只回放，追求接近 100% 的缓存命中率；
  2. 双层额度熔断：配置每日调用额度与单次运行额度，触顶立即停下并告警，额度可在设置页动态调整；
  3. 分诊降本：规则直判 + 历史人审结论复用，把绝大多数重复失败挡在调用大模型之前。

九、上线前自查清单（Checklist）

在你的团队正式把这套 AI E2E 测试体系接进发布门禁前，可以用下面这份清单做最后一次体检：

  • 接入层：本地开发是否已通过 npx e2e login 订阅或低成本方式跑通？CI 流水线是否已强制锁定为「只回放、不自愈」？
  • 探索与回归分工：是否把 e2e explore AI 随机探索测试放在独立任务中用于排雷，而不混淆进严格的需求门禁？
  • 需求溯源：每条正式用例是否都有「逐字可查」的 PRD 原文依据，且有自动化硬闸拦截编造引用和 agent.assert？
  • 数据与路由健壮性：测试数据是否经接口独立准备、收尾抗乐观锁并发、ETag 带引号？动态 ID 是否已规避 36 进制并加上了路由比对单测？
  • 审计与防伪：CI 是否禁止在同一 PR 同时改录像和改断言？高风险核心流程是否都配了至少一条故障注入反例？
  • 平台自测：部署到服务器后，是否专门验收过测试平台自身——包括分诊 Agent 的显式只读路径权限、并发清理冲突、Flaky 误判边界与凭据脱敏扫描？

做到这一步，你得到的不再是一堆「偶尔能跑、随时可能胡说八道」的 AI 演示脚本，而是一套用 AI 极大拉低编写与维护成本、同时用确定性工程锁死质量底线的现代端到端测试基础设施。

entry.title: 不露脸，1个月，涨粉6.37万！我用AI复刻了YouTube黑马账号的470万播放爆款
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @Leviwoyun（Levi 卧云） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

一篇给新手小白的 AI 动画复刻实战教程

一个不露脸的动画频道，没有真人出镜，没有复杂的拍摄设备

仅仅用动画讲述各种脑洞大开的 What If 故事

起号约1个月，发布39条视频，涨粉63,700，累计播放突破980万

其中一条视频播放量超过470万

这就是我最近拆解的 YouTube 频道：Ifverse（@IfverseTales）

它的内容形式很有意思：

如果你的反应速度快10倍，会发生什么？

如果你的智商达到500，会发生什么？

如果一秒钟感觉像十年，会发生什么？

它把这些普通人都能理解的假设，变成有视觉冲击力、有故事情节的动画

我研究了一下，发现这类频道有一个值得借鉴的内容公式：

What If + 极端能力/条件 + 具体场景 + 意想不到的结果

这种内容不需要真人出镜，也不需要复杂的三维动画制作

那么，能不能借助AI，把类似的动画视频制作出来？

我决定亲自使用 Renoise App，从爆款拆解、角色设计、分镜、视频生成，到配音、音效、剪辑和最终导出，完整跑通一次制作流程。最终完成了31秒的AI复刻视频，以及原片和复刻片的上下屏对比视频，先看效果。

说明：原视频约7分12秒，本次只复刻了前31.125秒，主要验证场景、构图、机位、人物动作、镜头节奏和音视频衔接。

下面把整个过程拆开，新手小白零动画制作经验也可以跟着操作

一、第一步：找到值得复刻的爆款频道

不要一上来就让AI帮你生成动画，先找到一个已经被市场验证的内容样本

这次我选择的是 Ifverse，我主要观察了几个方面：

  1. 频道的起号时间和发布数量
  2. 近期视频的播放表现
  3. 爆款视频的标题和封面
  4. 视频开头的叙事方式
  5. 人物造型、画面风格和动画表现形式

其中，我选择了这条视频作为复刻对象：

What If Your Reaction Time Was 10x Faster?

中文意思：如果你的反应速度快10倍，会发生什么？

原视频约7分12秒，最高播放量超过470万

为什么选它？因为它有几个特点：

  • 主题简单，普通人一眼就能理解
  • 场景生活化，主要发生在咖啡馆
  • 人物造型简单，适合AI生成
  • 动作有明显的视觉表现，例如苍蝇飞过、伸手接住咖啡杯
  • 镜头之间有明确的动作衔接

对于第一次尝试AI动画复刻的新手小白来说，这种素材比复杂的多人打斗、场景切换更容易入手。我的建议是先找一条场景简单、角色不多、动作清晰的爆款视频，不要一开始就挑战复杂动画。

二、第二步：让AI拆解原视频

找到参考视频之后，不要直接把链接扔给AI，让它生成一条类似的视频

先做镜头拆解，我把原视频导入分析流程，让AI按照时间轴逐镜头分析

重点提取以下信息：

  • | 分析维度 | 需要提取的内容 |
  • | :—————- | :—————- |
  • | 时间轴 | 每个镜头的开始和结束时间 |
  • | 场景 | 人物在哪里，周围有什么 |
  • | 景别 | 远景、中景、近景、特写 |
  • | 机位 | 正面、侧面、俯拍、仰拍 |
  • | 人物 | 人物的位置、动作、表情 |
  • | 运镜 | 固定、推近、拉远、旋转 |
  • | 声音 | 旁白、对白、环境音、音效 |
  • | 衔接 | 镜头切换的时间和方式 |

这里有一个非常重要的细节，不要只分析画面，还要分析动作发生的时间点

比如：

人物什么时候举手？咖啡杯什么时候倾斜？

杯子什么时候掉落？主角什么时候伸手接住？

这些时间点如果不准确，最终生成的视频即使画风接近，也会失去原片的节奏。以下是我使用的分析提示词：

完成拆解之后，我没有直接生成31秒视频，而是把它分成了三个独立片段

  • | 片段 | 时间 | 主要内容 |
  • | :— | :— | :— |
  • | A段 | 0～10秒 | 苍蝇飞过，主角快速抓住苍蝇 |
  • | B段 | 10～20秒 | 朋友碰倒咖啡杯，主角伸手接住 |
  • | C段 | 20～31秒 | 朋友惊讶，进一步解释正常人的反应速度 |

总计约31.125秒，15个镜头，这样拆分，后续生成、修改和检查都会容易很多

三、第三步：设计可以长期复用的动画角色

接下来是角色设计，如果每次生成视频，人物长相、颜色、服装都不一样，频道就很难形成统一的视觉风格。所以，我没有让AI直接生成视频，而是先设计了两名固定角色。

这次设计了两个原创角色：

角色一：DASH（主角）

  • 黑色极简火柴人
  • 圆形黑色头部
  • 白色眼睛和微笑
  • 右手佩戴青绿色护腕
  • 青绿色运动鞋

角色二：MILO（朋友）

  • 灰色火柴人
  • 珊瑚红色针织帽
  • 白色圆框眼镜
  • 深灰色运动鞋

两个人物的轮廓、颜色和配饰都固定下来，后续所有视频都使用同一套角色设定图。

角色设计提示词

这里有个小技巧，角色设定图不要只生成一张好看的图片，最好同时生成三视图和常用表情，后面制作视频时，把角色设定图作为参考素材一起上传。

四、第四步：使用 Renoise App 生成动画

前面的准备工作完成后，正式进入视频制作，这次的主要工具是 Renoise ai

我选择使用它的AI创作流程，将参考视频、角色设定图和分镜提示词结合起来。整个过程可以理解为：**原片参考 + 角色参考 + 分镜提示词 → AI生成视频。**具体操作如下：

1. 导入参考素材，准备两份素材：

  • 原视频片段：提供场景、构图、机位、动作和镜头节奏参考
  • 角色设定图：提供固定的人物外观参考

注意，两份素材的作用不同。原视频负责告诉AI应该怎么拍，角色设定图负责告诉AI人物应该长什么样。

2. 编写视频生成提示词

我没有简单地告诉AI，帮我复刻这个视频

而是把每个镜头的具体要求写进提示词，主要包括

  • 视频比例和时长
  • 画面风格
  • 场景和光线
  • 人物位置
  • 镜头运动
  • 每个镜头的起止时间
  • 人物具体动作
  • 声音和音效
  • 不允许出现的内容

视频生成提示词模板

实际制作时，需要根据每个镜头的具体情况补充动作和时间点，不能直接照搬这个模板就期待得到完全一致的结果。

3. 分段生成，不要一次生成整条视频

这是我这次实测中比较重要的经验，我把31秒视频分成了三个任务

  • A段：10秒，6个镜头
  • B段：10秒，5个镜头
  • C段：11秒，4个镜头

本次使用 Seedance 2.5 Flash，先以480P生成样片，每完成一个片段，就和原片逐镜头对比，确认通过后，再进入下一个片段。这样做有三个好处

  1. 某个镜头不满意，只需要处理对应片段
  2. 不会因为修改一个镜头而重新生成整条视频
  3. 可以更精确地控制镜头时间和人物动作

本次实际生成消耗：

  • | 项目 | 积分 |
  • | :— | —: |
  • | A段 | 50 |
  • | B段 | 50 |
  • | C段 | 55 |
  • | 视频生成合计 | 155 |

这是本次样片的实际消耗，不代表其他任务的固定价格。另外，聊天、构思和修改方案与实际生成素材是不同的计费环节，生成和剪辑的费用以App当时显示为准。

4. 每段生成后都要检查

不要看到AI提示生成成功，就认为任务完成了，我每段都会检查

  • 人物外观有没有变化
  • 场景和背景是否一致
  • 人物左右位置是否正确
  • 动作是否完整
  • 镜头切换时间是否准确
  • 有没有多余人物、物体和文字

尤其要注意手部动作，比如这次B段，主角接咖啡杯的动作，必须让观众清楚看到杯子落下、手掌接住、杯子稳定停在手中。如果动作没有完整表现出来，就需要重新调整对应镜头。

五、第五步：配音和音效处理

画面生成完成之后，还需要处理声音，这部分千万不要忽略

一条动画视频的声音至少包括：

  1. 旁白
  2. 人物对白
  3. 环境音
  4. 动作音效
  5. 背景音乐

这次复刻的旁白和对白，都是按照原片的内容和时间轴安排的。具体如下：

  • | 时间 | 角色 | 英文台词 |
  • | :— | :— | :— |
  • | 0.80～2.52秒 | 旁白 | A fly buzzes past your face. |
  • | 3.78～4.48秒 | 旁白 | You don’t even think. |
  • | 5.00～6.64秒 | 旁白 | You just catch it. |
  • | 10.91～12.71秒 | 旁白 | Your friend knocks his coffee off the table. |
  • | 13.61～15.11秒 | 旁白 | The cup hasn’t even started to fall, |
  • | 15.41～18.51秒 | 旁白 | and your hand is already under it. |
  • | 22.79～24.49秒 | Milo | How? How did you do that? |
  • | 25.45～30.25秒 | 旁白 | A normal human reacts in about a quarter of a second. |

我把旁白和Milo的对白分开生成，保证两个人的声音能够区分。音效怎么处理？这次使用了

  • 咖啡馆环境音
  • 苍蝇飞过的声音
  • 手部动作的Whoosh音效
  • 咖啡杯碰撞声
  • 咖啡杯落入手掌的轻响
  • 秒表滴答声

还有一个很容易被忽略的问题，环境音和音效不能盖过旁白

我最初生成的版本，开头几秒的环境音和音效明显太大，听起来甚至有些嘈杂。后来把旁白、环境音和音效分开处理，重新调整音量比例，才得到最终确认的版本。建议

  • 旁白始终保持清晰
  • 人物说话时，自动降低背景音
  • 音效只在对应动作发生时出现
  • 不要重复叠加原片自带的旁白
  • 最后一定要戴耳机完整听一遍

六、第六步：最终剪辑和上下屏对比

三个片段生成、配音和音效完成后，就可以进入最终剪辑。这一步主要做：

  1. 按照A→B→C的顺序拼接
  2. 检查三个片段的切点
  3. 统一画面色调
  4. 统一黑边和画面比例
  5. 添加英文字幕
  6. 添加原片中的0.25 s秒表文字
  7. 对齐旁白、对白和音效
  8. 完整播放检查

这次最终视频时长为31.125秒

最后，我又制作了一条上下屏对比视频

上半屏：470万播放的爆款原片，下半屏：AI复刻版

两条视频从第一帧同步播放，原片静音，复刻片保留完整声音

这种对比方式很适合做教程展示，观众可以直接看到：

  • 场景是否一致
  • 人物动作是否接近
  • 镜头切换是否对齐
  • 画面风格是否接近
  • AI生成还有哪些不足

这比单独展示一条AI生成视频更有说服力

七、这次实战，我总结了5个经验

1. 先拆解，再生成

不要把所有希望寄托在一段提示词上。分镜、人物动作、时间点越明确，后续生成越容易控制。

2. 角色设定图非常重要

固定人物的外观、配色、服装和配饰，才能让多个视频保持一致

3. 尽量分段生成

先从10秒左右的片段开始，确认效果后再继续

4. 画面和声音要分开检查

视频生成成功，不代表声音也合格。旁白、环境音和音效需要单独处理

5. 不要迷信一键生成

AI可以帮你完成大量工作，但镜头检查、动作纠正、时间轴调整和最终剪辑，仍然需要人工把关。

这次31秒的复刻，也不是逐帧完全一致。部分人物动作、手部细节和画面元素仍然存在差异。但从场景、构图、机位、人物位置到主要动作节奏，已经跑通了完整的AI复刻流程。

对于没有动画制作经验的新手小白来说，这个结果已经足够说明，AI可以大幅降低动画内容制作的入门门槛。

八、工具入口与活动

这次实战使用的是 Renoise App，我比较看重它的一点是，不只提供素材生成，还能把Agent创作、配音、剪辑和成片导出串联起来。

对于不懂代码、没有专业动画制作经验的人，可以从一条30秒左右的短片开始，逐步熟悉整个制作流程。

Renoise 专属体验链接：

https://renoise.onelink.me/Gxyb?pid=xcom&c=daodao166888-chen-202611&af_web_dp=https%3A%2F%2Frenoise.ai%2F%3Futm_medium%3Dxcom%26utm_source%3Ddaodao166888-chen-202611

另外，Renoise 黑五活动已经开始：

  • 活动时间：11月18日～12月1日
  • 月付：首月最高7折
  • 年付：首年最高5折

具体优惠以活动页面显示为准，最后说一句：

我的目标一直很简单，**让没有动画制作经验的新手小白，也能借助AI做出自己的爆款视频。**先拆解一个爆款，先完成30秒样片，再逐步把这套流程变成自己可以重复使用的生产SOP，这才是AI工具真正值得研究的地方。

entry.title: Mode Engineering: Stop Paying a Top Model for Every Step
entry.content:
本文转载自 X 博主 @rincyXIII（rincy） 的长文，原文链接，版权归原作者所有。

How to give every piece of work the right amount of intelligence: the mode per channel, the script for the fixed steps, and the run that never needed to happen

In 2024 Sam Altman posted four words that every AI builder remembers

Tokens did get cheaper

Running AI every day did not get simple

Because the price of a token was never the real problem

The real problem is what you send to the most expensive model

The daily report

The ticket tagging

The hourly check that finds nothing 23 hours a day

The sum of a column

The date format

The “is there anything new” question asked again and again

None of those need a top model

Most automations send them to one anyway

Boris Cherny, who created Claude Code, wrote the new rule in one line

Number two is the one nobody engineers

How much effort

Not per prompt

Per place, per job, per step

That is mode engineering

This article is about building that split with an AI employee who already has every lever in it: Viktor

The expensive mistake inside every automation

An automation looks simple from the outside

Zoom in and it is a chain of small steps

Take the most common one there is: the morning revenue report

Five steps with one right answer

Two that need a model

When the whole thing runs as one AI run, the model does all seven

That creates four problems

The model does the arithmetic

It reads 40 rows into context and sums them in its head

A script does that for free and never gets it wrong

The run happens on empty days

Nothing closed on Sunday

The model still opened the CRM, pulled zero rows, reasoned about it, and wrote “no new deals”

You paid for a full run to learn nothing

The mode was set once, a long time ago

Someone built the report on the strongest model because it worked

It still runs on it, every day, for three lines

Nobody owns the choice

“Which model should I use for this?” gets answered per person, per day, from memory

The answer drifts

And the person typing is the worst person to answer it, because they are busy doing the actual work

The deeper problem is architectural

Judgment and plumbing have been collapsed into the same run

Mode engineering begins by separating them

Four kinds of work

Every step in every job falls into one of four boxes

Judgment a human reads

Strategy questions

A reply to an upset customer

A launch post

A brief from a messy thread

Quality is visible here and mistakes are public

Give it the strong mode

Routine a human reads

The daily digest

The standup summary

The ticket triage note

A human reads it, but the shape is the same every day

Give it a cheaper mode and check that it still holds

Work nobody reads as prose

Tagging

Sorting

Pulling fields into a sheet

Yes / no checks that feed the next step

You are paying for sentences nobody sees

Give it the cheapest mode

One right answer

  • Sums
  • Queries
  • Dates
  • Thresholds

“Did anything change since the last run”

This is not a model job at all

Give it a script

Most teams have only one box

Everything goes to the model they like best

Viktor is built for this split

Viktor is an AI employee

He lives in Slack, Microsoft Teams and email. He connects to 9,800+ tools. He has his own computer in the cloud where he writes and runs code

79,000+ teams have hired him

Two things make him the right place to do mode engineering

  • He is multi-model
    The mode is a setting on the employee, not a second subscription. The hard question and the daily digest go to the same hire, on different modes
  • He writes code
    The steps with one right answer can leave the model and become a script he set up himself, in the same workspace, with the same tools

The model choice has been in the product since February. His co-founder announced it with the detail that matters most

Cost you can see before the run is the first half of mode engineering

The second half is deciding it once, so nobody has to look at a badge fifty times a day

One honest line before the setup, because everything below depends on it

Viktor does not choose the mode for each task by himself. You set the defaults. He works on the mode the place or the task is set to, and anyone can override it when the default is wrong

That is the point

The choice gets made once, by the person who knows the work

Lever 1: Set the mode once per place

Viktor’s model settings have four layers, from his settings docs

The layer that does the most work is the channel

Why the channel is the right unit

Work already sorts itself by channel

#research gets hard questions

**#standup **gets summaries

**#intake **gets things to tag and route

Setting the mode per channel matches the effort to the work without anyone thinking about it

Nobody picks a model in #standup

They just ask Viktor in the channel where the work belongs

The dialog shows its own cost

When an admin changes channel default models, the dialog shows the credits each channel spent over the last 30 days and an estimate of the monthly change

You see the effect before you press save

That is the opposite of how most teams change models: switch, wait for the invoice, guess

Old threads keep their model

A thread that already has its own model keeps it when the channel default changes

New threads pick up the new default

So the change is safe mid-week. It takes effect as new work starts

The best routing rule in the docs

The docs do not say which model sits behind each mode

They give something more useful: one sentence about scheduled tasks that is worth copying everywhere

Viktor defaults to smart. You can ask for balanced for lower-cost routine work, or cheap for runs that write nothing people read

“Write nothing people read”

That is the whole routing logic in five words

If a human reads the output, quality is visible and a mistake costs you

If nobody does, you are paying for prose that goes straight into a sheet

Here is how I would map a team

Five settings

After that, picking a model stops being part of anyone’s day

The exceptions are one word

Sometimes a message in a Balanced channel deserves more

!fast runs one reply on the workspace’s fast model

!deep runs one reply on the workspace’s deep model

Admins choose which models those are under Model overrides. Every reply says what it ran on in its footer, so nobody has to guess afterwards

Admins can also add custom commands that pin a model, a reasoning level and a speed, up to 10 per workspace

This is what “I stopped picking models” means in practice

The choice still exists

You only make it when the default is wrong

Lever 2: Stop the runs that have nothing to do

The cheapest run is the one that never starts

And there are a lot of runs that should never start

Look at what teams actually use an AI employee for over time. The team behind Viktor shared their own numbers last month

Teams build first, then keep him around to watch

That is the right instinct

It is also where empty runs live

A monitor asks “did anything change?” on a schedule

Most of the time the answer is no

If every one of those questions is a full AI run, the bill grows with the clock, not with the work

The condition script

Viktor’s scheduled-tasks docs describe exactly this fix

He can add “a condition script that runs before each scheduled run and skips the run when there is nothing to do”

The question “is there anything new?” has one right answer

So it goes to code

The model only wakes up when there is something to think about

The warning worth listening to

The docs add one more detail: Viktor warns when an AI task would run more than about six times a day

If you see that warning, the task is usually a condition script waiting to be written

Ask for it in one message

That last line matters

Every action that matters waits for a yes from you. A task that quietly stopped posting is not a saving

Lever 3: Move the fixed steps into code

This is the lever with the biggest effect

It is also the one most teams never pull

Boris Cherny made the case for it in July, about Claude Code, and it applies to every automation

Read that again with a daily report in mind

The model could sum the deals every morning

That uses tokens and might get it wrong

Or the sum can become code once, and be right forever

Three shapes of a recurring job

Viktor can run a recurring job in three shapes, from his scheduled-tasks docs

He writes the scripts himself, on his own computer in the cloud. You describe the job in chat, he sets it up

He also writes a plain-language explanation of every new or changed script, so a non-engineer can read what it does before saying yes

The morning report, rebuilt

The model still does the part that needs a model

It stopped doing the arithmetic, the fetching and the empty-day check

And because it now gets five numbers instead of 40 rows, the run it does make is shorter

The ask

Jobs with no judgment at all

Some jobs have no judgment step

“Copy yesterday’s signups into the sheet and post the count”

There is nothing to decide

That job should not start an AI run. It becomes a script task

The same split for events

Event triggers start work when something happens: a CRM event, a webhook, a message in a channel

Viktor’s trigger docs describe two handlers. One runs Viktor with your instructions. One runs a Python script, which “suits high-volume events”

A webhook that fires 500 times a day where 490 need no thought belongs to the script handler

And for periodic checks, the docs say a scheduled task “is usually cheaper, and Viktor may suggest one”

Where code is the wrong answer

Scripts remove one failure class. They add another

  • Script cannot notice the unusual
    If the CRM renames a field, the sum is wrong and the script does not know. Keep a check in the AI step: “if the numbers look off by more than 3x, say so instead of writing the report”
  • Scripts have limits
    Script handler on an event trigger stops after 10 minutes and pauses itself after three timed-out runs in a row. A paused job is a report nobody gets
  • Judgment does not become an if-statement
    “Decide what is worth saying” written as code becomes a report that says the same thing every day

Keep the model on the part that needs a model

Move everything else

The checkup: ask him where the credits go

Here is the step everyone skips

They set the modes, it feels cheaper, and they never look

With Viktor, looking is one message in any conversation

From his usage docs, this is what he can answer in chat

Two limits worth knowing

He only reads this data. Plan and credit changes go through the Billing page, by an admin

He does not give a ready-made forecast for when credits run out. He compares your balance with your recent daily spend, which is honest, and enough to see trouble coming

Per-teammate and per-Space breakdowns are for admins. Admins also get a direct message at 70% and 90% of the workspace’s credits, unless auto top-ups are on

Read the answer like a bug report

The answer is almost always lopsided

A few things cost most of the credits

So the question is not “how do we spend less”

It is “what are the top three, and which lever fits each one”

Then let him propose the fix

You approve what makes sense

You keep the receipts for the next section

The Usage page is the receipt

The chat checkup is the quick version

The Usage page is the proof

From Viktor’s usage docs: admins see it for the last 30 days or the current billing period. Summary cards, a daily spend chart, and the costs of conversations and scheduled tasks. Depending on the workspace, there are views per teammate, per scheduled task and per Space

The scheduled-tasks view sorts by total credits, total runs or last activity

That sort is the whole audit

Do it the week before a change and the week after

Same five steps. Same three numbers

That is the only honest way to say “we spend less”

Not “it feels cheaper”

Before and after, from the same page

The 15-task mode test

A mode map on paper is a guess

Run it against real work before the team relies on it

Fifteen tasks the team actually does, each sent in the channel it would normally go to

For each one, write down four things

Then read the results by mode, not by task

If everything passes on the cheap modes

Your map is too generous somewhere. Move one channel down and rerun its tasks

If writing fails on Balanced

Move those channels to Smart. Writing a human reads is where a lower mode shows first

If data needs !deep to get the numbers right

That is usually a sign the numbers should not come from a model at all. Lever 3

If D3 and D4 pass on Cheap

That is the expected result. A classification and a yes / no. That is the shape of most recurring jobs, and the shape that saves the most once it runs every day

Save the 15 prompts in a doc. Rerun them after any change to the map

A map that passed last month is not proof for next month

The bill outside the employee

Half of the AI bill is not in Viktor at all

It is the subscriptions the team collected before

When the work goes through one AI employee, some of that stops being used

Not all of it. Be precise about which

Cancel what nobody used in the last 30 days

Keep what someone uses for work Viktor does not do for your team. There usually is something, and that is fine

When you still pick the model yourself

The honest section

A mode map handles the normal day. It does not handle everything

The hard question in the wrong channel

A strategy question in #standup, which runs on Balanced

Use !deep, or ask it in the channel set to Ultra

The default is for the usual, not the exception

Writing that will be published

A launch post. A reply to an upset customer. A page on the website

I would not leave those to a lower mode to save a few credits

The cost of a bad sentence in public is higher than the cost of a better model

Work you do not understand yet

The first week of a new kind of job, run it on Smart

Move it down once you know what good output looks like and you can see the lower mode still produces it

A task that started failing

If a task on Balanced or Cheap starts producing output people complain about, move it up first and debug second

Your own experiments

Some people keep a personal subscription to try new models the day they ship

That is a personal choice

It does not need to be a team bill

The math

There is no Viktor pricing in this article, on purpose. Prices change, and they live on Viktor’s own page

The math does not need prices

It needs a formula and your own Usage page

Every lever changes exactly one term

There’s an argument that perpetual futures are one of the greatest inventions to come out of the crypto industry.

Access to leverage with no expiry on a single orderbook via dangerously intuitive interfaces has turned into a market that does roughly $80-$90 trillion in annual volume.

However, as the industry has matured, there’s still been no major breakthrough from any other trading instrument, most notably options.

Every asset class, from equities to commodities, started off as a spot-dominated market, but as it matured, options almost always became the dominant trading derivative.

The reason is that options give traders flexibility. Traders can configure a whole suite of customized multi-leg strategies depending on their thesis. They get configurable convexity.

But in crypto, this configurable convexity comes at a cost.

First of all, options are complicated, especially for an average shitcoin trader like you or me. Straddles, covered calls, iron condors, butterflies, and the different Greek terms - it’s a bit too much.

But beyond the complexity is the technical design of the instrument. Options come with multiple expiries, something that’s been proven difficult to make sense of in a 24/7 market. Plus, it comes with multiple strike prices.

If I, as a trader, am looking to buy a call on ETH, I see a $1.5k strike, a $1.75k strike, and a $2k strike, with liquidity fragmented across these strike prices.

Once you bring in more traders and more money to this fragmented environment, trade execution is almost always suboptimal, especially onchain.

So okay, perps have the upper hand when it comes to simplicity and liquidity. However, when you’re looking to get higher upside on a high-conviction trade, perps are still limited.

You may open a 2x long on ETH at $1.8k based on a certain thesis. Then you read a Vitalik blog post, for example, which only furthers your conviction in this trade. This is the trade that will finally get you out of the trenches, you think to yourself.

Trying to increase your upside means adding more leverage. So you make this position a 3x or 5x leverage long.

What is effectively happening is that you’re adding more risk to your trade for the same linear payoff. You aren’t increasing exposure, you’re simply increasing risk.

If ETH pumps 20% from here, so does your ETH-PERP. But one bad wick and your liquidation price is now higher than before.

So what’s the bottom line?

Your convexity shouldn’t come with a deadline, and your thesis shouldn’t have an expiry date.

What if there were a product that offered the simple, liquid, and continuous exposure of perps with the convexity of options? Does that sound like something you’re interested in? Well, I kinda am.

So let’s dive into the ABCs of Power Perps.

What is a Power Perp?

Thesis: Power Perps give traders the convexity of options with the simplicity and enhanced liquidity of perps. No strikes, no expiries, one unified market.

A Power Perp is an instrument that trades similarly to a regular perp contract while simultaneously giving you option-like exposure without strike prices or expiries.

It’s a contract where the payoff is non-linear because, instead of tracking the underlying asset’s price 1:1, it squares, cubes, or raises the underlying asset’s price to the fourth power, creating a completely new payoff and exposure dynamic.

Allow me to elaborate with an example.

If you’re trading a regular ETH-PERP, your payoff is linear. If ETH (the underlying) goes to 2x, your ETH-PERP goes 2x.

With a Power Perp, you’re trading ETH², so if ETH (the underlying) pumps 2x, your Power Perp goes 4x, if ETH goes 3x, your Power Perp goes 9x, and so on.

Higher powers make this effect even more extreme. A cubed Power Perp means a 2x pump is actually 8x, while a power of 4 turns the same move into a 16x.

It’s like auto-compounding exposure. As the price of the underlying increases, your exposure automatically increases, giving you higher upside via non-linear payoff. Thus, we say, Power Perps give you the convexity of options with the simplicity of perps.

A product like this is perfectly suited for crypto’s volatile nature.

It’s not benefiting from volatility in the same way an options straddle would, where the direction doesn’t matter (although you can mimic a straddle with a combination of Power Perps).

You most certainly want to be correct on your thesis/direction, but large, volatile moves perfectly interact with the convex payoff.

  • ETH pumps 5%, ETH² Power Perp pumps 10.25%
  • ETH pumps 20%, ETH² Power Perp pumps 44%
  • ETH pumps 50%, ETH² Power Perp pumps 125%

The larger the move, the more convexity helps you. So, if the move is in your direction, Power Perps offer significantly more upside in high-volatility environments.

How does the market actually work?

Now that the scalability of onchain infrastructure has reached a point where orderbooks can function seamlessly, the game for derivatives has changed.

The main benefit Power Perps have over options, especially onchain, is unified liquidity.

As stated before, if you wanted convex exposure to ETH onchain, it would have to be through DeFi options, where liquidity would be in vaults or liquidity pools, and that already low liquidity would be fragmented across the various strike prices and expiries.

With Power Perps, liquidity is concentrated into one orderbook. Everyone trades in one unified ETH² market.

Plus, the orderbook gives you unified liquidity with familiarity.

It trades in an orderbook just like any other ETH-PERP would, and the long/short structure remains the same. If Alice is looking to long ETH2, her counterparty, Bob, will short ETH² in the same book.

Things take a bit of a turn when it comes to funding.

Like linear perps, funding for Power Perps will usually lean towards **longs paying shorts. **It can be thought of as the price for convexity, kinda like how option sellers collect premiums.

The reason for this lean comes from the payoff itself. Let’s take a simple example:

  • If ETH goes up 10%, ETH² goes up 21%
  • If ETH goes down 10%, ETH² goes down 19%

The long side has more value because the squared term is always positive. With larger upward moves, your exposure increases, and so do your gains. But someone has to be willing to provide that convexity.

So the short is effectively saying, I’ll give you that convex exposure, but you have to pay me for it. You pay funding to own convexity, and you hope the move you receive is large enough to justify the cost.

When the underlying is flat, for example, it’s the shorts collecting the funding that win, but if the long thesis plays out, then increased exposure and upside will be worth the cost.

What all of this culminates in is Power Perps creating a new payoff shape.

As the image earlier in this article showed, Power Perps create a curved payoff rather than a linear one. This changes your exposure.

A simple way to think of it is that a normal perp has a fixed exposure, while a Power Perp dynamically changes its exposure with the price of the underlying.

For example:

  • As price rises, your sensitivity to further upside increases. A +10% move produces +21%, +50% produces +125%, and +100% produces +300% - Upward moves compound exposure
  • As price falls, your sensitivity to further downside shrinks. A -10% move produces -19%, while -50% produces -75% rather than -100%. - Downward moves reduce your exposure

You automatically become more exposed as the market rises and less exposed as it falls, creating a completely unique payoff shape that the world of crypto derivatives hasn’t seen yet, at least at a highly scalable level.

Any portfolio of assets with a payoff represented as a continuous function can be represented as a portfolio of Power Perpetuals.

So instead of constructing a complicated portfolio of different derivatives, you can construct your desired payoff using Power Perps as the underlying building blocks.

For example, you can:

  • Long a Power Perp
  • Long call options
  • Create a straddle-like position
  • Hedge for Uniswap LP

Things get a lot more interesting if you conceptualize implementing Power Perps into the current onchain environment.

Let’s take something like Hyperliquid, a mature onchain perp DEX with well-capitalized, sophisticated market makers and portfolio margin.

Say a market maker has $10 million in BTC/ETH as collateral or inventory already on Hyperliquid. That liquidity can be used to create a short Power Perp position without having to put up a completely separate pool of capital.

With portfolio margin, the margin system considers the entire portfolio when assessing risk, so in this case, it will count BTC, ETH, and short Power Perp all in one, rather than as isolated risk positions.

This, therefore, incentivizes market makers to short Power Perps as they can consistently collect funding from those looking for convex upside exposure.

Even though the short side is naturally riskier, portfolio margin allows market makers to do it with existing capital, making their system more efficient.

The result is creating natural short-side liquidity. This liquidity then makes it easier for all the longers willing to pay for convex exposure to trade.

This product probably sounds familiar… ahem ahem Squeeth

Those of you who have been around for a while probably remember how big a rage Squeeth was in 2021, when DeFi activity was at its peak.

Squeeth was a product from Opyn and the first Power Perp to hit the market. It worked much like what we described above in this article, but after launching in 2021 with some success, it was completely shut down by November 2024.

So what happened?

The ultimate problem for Squeeth was that it was too illiquid and too DeFi-native, using AMMs (instead of CLOBs) and vaults. Too many derivative tokens and loops and pools to jump through.

The primary trading venue for Squeeth’s tradable token oSQTH was the oSQTH/ETH pool on Uniswap.

To provide liquidity, you would of course need both tokens, which proved to be problematic for LPs as the payoff was non-linear.

LPs would technically be accumulating the underperforming asset (ETH) mechanically and selling some of the outperforming asset (oSQTH). Your classic impermanent loss issue. Hence, low liquidity.

Then there was the vault issue. Someone who wanted to mint/short Squeeth could only do so by locking collateral in an Opyn vault.

That capital would essentially become frozen and tedious to manage, something that would dissuade a lot of liquidity from entering the system.

Then you have the funding issue. During major volatility events, like The Merge, for example, funding rates could spike to 0.4%-0.5%, making it difficult to use as a hedge.

So ultimately, too complicated, too many loops, and an inefficient design made it difficult to attract liquidity at scale, which resulted in the product being subpar for traders, and therefore eventually led to Squeeth’s sunsetting.

What’s different this time around?

You’ve probably heard the saying, “It’s not about who did it first, it’s about who did it right.” Well, that saying couldn’t be any more applicable here.

Sometimes, an innovation is just too early. The underlying infrastructure may not be ready to support it at scale, and maybe the market just isn’t in the correct place for it to take off.

Power Perps in 2021 were a cool innovation on an inefficient protocol design that wasn’t scalable. Now, the market is ripe for a product like this.

Onchain orderbooks allow for unified liquidity on a familiar interface, solving the major user-facing hurdles. But beyond that, the crypto market has matured to a point where the surrounding use cases of Power Perps have genuine potential to attract users and liquidity.

1. Dynamic exposure

Unlike normal perps, your exposure changes as the underlying moves. A squared underlying makes the instrument more sensitive to price moves.

You have an ETH² Power Perp position. Let’s say the current ETH price is $1,000. At this point, your exposure to the Power Perp is 2x.

Now ETH pumps to $1,500. Your exposure becomes 3x. Then it continues pumping to $2,000, your exposure becomes 4x. Your exposure grows as ETH’s price grows.

But let’s look at the flipside. ETH is at $1,000, and you have 2x exposure. Then ETH falls to $500, and your exposure is 1x. As the price goes down, your exposure shrinks.

This is the essence of dynamic exposure. It’s like having an auto-rebalancing position where, instead of constantly increasing or decreasing leverage manually, your exposure changes in line with the price movement of the underlying asset.

2. Different liquidation profile

The dynamic exposure element directly correlates to how the liquidation profile for Power Perps is different.

The best way to understand it is to compare it to a regular perp.

Say you have a 3x long ETH-PERP. You enter at $1,500, and the price falls to $1,250, then $1,000, then $750, and then $500. Since leverage here is constant, every $250 drop in ETH will affect your position the same.

With a Power Perp, this same drop in price causes the position’s delta to drop with it, so each additional dollar of ETH downside has a smaller effect on your position.

You can think of it as a kind of self-deleveraging mechanism as the price moves down.

This is not to say that you can’t get liquidated or that your downside is capped. You can very much get liquidated, depending on your margin, funding, entry price, and so on. But the exposure change makes liquidations a bit different here.

3. Concentrated convexity

Another attractive feature comes from a simple and intuitive product design.

Rather than trying to spread convexity across different strike prices, different expiries, multiple venues, and different pools, you get it all packaged under one roof.

One market, one instrument, one orderbook. That’s concentrated convexity.

4. Funding

With Power Perps, funding is both a cost and a feature.

It’s a cost, well, because longers must be willing to pay for the convexity, and they pay that cost through funding.

It’s a feature because it attracts people who want to earn that carry.

A market maker with idle collateral, or just another trader who may say, “I believe ETH is going to be stable through this period, and everyone else is wrong, so let me earn the funding through this Power Perp.”

Not only is it a great trade, but it also acts as a great way to attract more liquidity for the longers.

5. Directional conviction

As a trader, one of the most frustrating things is being correct about your thesis but still not making money on the trade.

You had the conviction, but your option came with an expiry, and maybe you had to readjust your trade accordingly. Maybe your thesis is playing out slowly, but you aren’t well-capitalized, so you don’t want to keep adding risk through leverage to increase your exposure.

Power Perps give you a little more freedom when you have directional conviction to not only let your trade play out, but also to get rewarded handsomely for it.

6. Capital efficiency

As an overall product, it’s simply more capital-efficient for everyone involved.

On one side, Power Perps turn directional conviction into dynamically increasing exposure, while giving traders a single perpetual instrument with concentrated convexity.

You don’t need to hop through pools or vaults, and you don’t need to worry about liquidity across different strikes.

On the other hand, if we come back to the BTC/ETH portfolio margin system, on the short side, it means Power Perps can interact with existing positions and don’t need a new pool of capital to be added.

Everyone wins, capital efficiency at its finest.

With all of that now said, let’s get into the actual practical implementation of bringing this product to market.

The team best suited to pull this off is Paragon.

Power Perps with Paragon

@tradeparagon is a market-creation layer on top of Hyperliquid that lets people trade perps on things that normally aren’t directly tradable onchain, i.e., individual stocks, market indices, treasury yields, crypto indices, themes, and potentially other assets.

Having facilitated more than $500 million in cumulative volume, Paragon is slowly establishing itself as a major up-and-comer among the Hyperliquid deployers.

The great thing is that for you, as the user, nothing changes. You trade directly on the Hyperliquid interface, and your money stays where it is.

The only thing is, Paragon is now set to differentiate itself significantly from the competition.

Yes, things like a BTC.D market and treasury yield markets are a great step in that direction. But we believe that introducing Power Perps on Hyperliquid will really catapult them to the next level.

So, how can you trade these Paragon Power Perps?

Well, just like you would any other perp on Hyperliquid.

  • Select the pair
  • Input your desired amount to trade
  • Make sure it’s the correct power
  • Place a trade

You will find all the options under the “para” subsection of the HIP-3 section of your Hyperliquid interface.

To make things easier for you, we’re also building a custom payoff simulator for Power Perps, that we’ll soon launch, so you can play around and know what to expect by simulating your trade before actually opening it.

Why now? Why Paragon?

The Power Perps we’re talking about right now aren’t vastly different from the ones we saw in 2021, from a technical standpoint.

The main difference is that we now have superior market infrastructure with the likes of Hyperledger to make such unique derivatives a widely traded market.

Given that Hyperliquid has a massive user base, an efficient orderbook, proven scalability, market makers, high liquidity, a mature perps trading environment, and established infrastructure, the delivery mechanism is there. All that’s left is implementation.

Hyperliquid has already proven that there is demand for novel onchain markets. Stocks, indices, ETFs, commodities, bonds, pre-IPO, and so on, all made possible by HIP-3.

The current onchain environment creates the perfect storm for Paragon to come in with Power Perps.

Paragon’s market curation thesis has always been offering traders the trades that they wish existed.

Whether it be a major crypto indicator like BTC dominance, which you couldn’t really trade before, or US 10Y or 30Y as a perp, or real-world tech/infra like Unitree. It’s all about turning what people wish into reality.

They’ve already seen a lot of success with their HIP-3 market deployments, and now, the stage is set for Power Perps.

Paragon will be the first to offer Hyperliquid traders Power Perps on majors like ETH and BTC, but this can eventually be applied to stocks, indices, indicators, macro assets, and so on.

A massive wave is coming, and it’s going to be a powerful perpetual one.

Risks

Now, as good as this product is, nothing comes without risks.

For starters, there’s the convexity angle. Yes, convexity on the upside is great, but it works both ways. Your exposure may technically decrease on the downside, but a large move against you can still result in large losses if not liquidation.

On top of this, the convexity isn’t free. On the long side, you will be paying more than usual through funding. If the market stays flat, you may lose to funding, but even in high-volatility environments, that convexity becomes valuable, and you may have to pay more to hold that position.

Then you have the question of leverage. Power Perps already have an element of embedded leverage through non-linear payoffs. On top of that, if some of you degens add more leverage to the position, it can become that much more sensitive.

This increases your chances of liquidation and large losses in major moves against you.

Another issue, at least early on, will be liquidity. Power Perps are relatively novel when compared to traditional perps.

The books are not going to be anywhere near as liquid to start off. So things like wider spreads, slippage, and price impact are expected early teething issues to be wary of.

As with perps and basically any other onchain product, oracle risk is always pertinent. The price of the underlying needs to be tracked accurately. Things like delayed oracle data feeds, oracle manipulation, incorrect data, oracle downtime, and so on could be potential problems.

Lastly, we have the ever-present risk of smart contracts. Whether it’s Paragon or any other onchain product, smart contract risk is always present. There’s always a non-zero chance that a smart contract can get hacked or exploited, so it’s always wise to practice appropriate risk management.

Concluding thoughts

With the regulatory side of things finally turning in the industry’s favor (somewhat), a lot of TradFi institutions have taken this as a green light and have started coming onchain with full force.

Despite how dry the markets may seem, it genuinely feels like crypto is having its “coming of age” moment.

Although it may take time, the market is responding well to novel products, and as the industry matures, these products will only continue to grow.

It’s about time that perps got a real competitor, and Power Perps with Paragon could be the one.

3、**来回切五六个软件磨一整天：**先找大模型写脚本分镜，再跑生图工具锁角色，再丢进图生视频抽卡，最后找配音、找配乐、找音效，拖进剪映对口型剪辑——辛辛苦苦磨一整天出一条 15 秒视频，发出去没爆，心态直接崩了。

起号拼的就是 稳定出片效率。为了让普通人不用懂复杂提示词、也不用切一堆工具就能批量出片，我最近把整套 3D 萌宠动画流程塞进了一个自带专用 Skill 的工具里实测了一遍——Renoise AI。

先不夸工具，直接看我按这套工作流一次跑出来的 15 秒完整 3D 萌宠成品《天上掉下来一朵云》（连中文童声台词、背景配乐和动作音效都是一次自带的）：

毛绒质感、四个角色的辨识度、故事起承转合，加上自带的台词和音效，直接发抖音、小红书或者视频号完全够打。下面我就把从零跑出这条片的完整 6 步操作，一步步拆给你看。

三、实操全流程：1 个 Skill，6 步直出 15 秒有声 3D 萌宠动画

整套操作几乎全是点选和大白话对话，哪怕你从来没写过英文 Prompt，照着下面 6 步也能直接上手：

第 1 步：打开 Skill 列表，选中「萌宠 3D 动画片」

打开工具后的对话界面，别直接瞎打字，先点输入框左侧那个「四瓣圆点」的技能图标。

在弹出的 Skill 列表里，找到并选中 萌宠 3D 动画片（卡片简介写得很直白：圆润可爱的电视动画 3D 质感，写下你的故事就能开拍）。这一步相当于直接帮你把整套 3D 渲染风格、镜头语言和声音管线都预设好了。

第 2 步：一句话说出想法，选定故事与 9:16 竖屏

选好 Skill 后，对话框会自动挂载对应的 3D 绘本动画指令 renoise-watercolor-picture-book-tv-cgi，你只需要像聊天一样发一句大白话：

我想制作一个萌宠3D的动画

紧接着系统会弹出一个交互式选故事卡片 萌宠 3D 动画：选个故事。

这里有两种玩法：你可以直接点选现成故事（我这次选的是 天上掉下来一朵云），也可以不选模板，直接打一句你想讲的原创剧情，甚至把主角换成你自己家的猫猫狗狗。

下方画面比例记得选 9:16 竖屏（适合抖音/小红书），一步适配短视频平台全屏观感。

第 3 步：核对 15 格分镜故事板（附防画成 2D 的关键避坑）

提交想法后，工具会自动吐出一张非常细的 15 格分镜故事板（15s STORYBOARD），精确到 每秒一格——每一秒的景别（远景/中景/特写）、场景、角色动作和台词全都排得明明白白。

**这一步有一个千万别跳过的检查点：**看分镜时一定要盯紧画风质感，确认它是你要的 3D 质感。如果偶尔抽风 画成了 2D 绘本风，千万别凑合着点下一步，直接在对话框里告诉它重画！在分镜阶段把画风卡死，后面出片才不会跑偏。

第 4 步：一键锁定 4 位主角定妆，彻底防角色崩坏

分镜敲定后，系统会自动生成一张包含所有主角的定妆效果图。这次的 4 个主角分别是橘猫 团团、小狗 豆豆、垂耳兔 跳跳 和 小云。

这一步的核心价值就是把 毛色、衣服、小配饰 全部一次性钉死——比如团团的红领巾和牛仔背带裤、豆豆的草绿针织马甲、跳跳的小花草帽和淡紫碎花裙。角色定妆锁好之后，后面 15 秒切十几个镜头，主角形象都能稳稳贴合，不再出现“下一秒换了只猫”的尴尬。

第 5 步：直接生成动画，一次直出 15 秒含台词、配乐、音效

分镜和角色都确认没问题，点击开始生成，剩下的渲染和剪辑就全部交给它自动跑完。

这一步最省时间的地方在于：它不是给你吐一堆零碎的 3 秒无声素材让你自己去剪映拼，而是一次直接出 15 秒完整连贯的成片，并且自动配齐了中文童声台词、背景配乐和场景音效。就是开头大家看到的那版《天上掉下来一朵云》。

第 6 步：指定瑕疵片段局部精修，不用全片推倒重做

做 AI 视频老手都知道，哪怕 95% 的画面都完美，只要有 1 秒穿模，整条片子质感就会掉一截。以前遇到这种事只能自认倒霉重抽，但这里可以直接 局部精修。

比如我这次成片里检查到 作品 3 有个小瑕疵：叠罗汉那段，小兔子跳跳举起小云时手臂位置很别扭。我直接选中 作品 3，在对话框里用大白话告诉它怎么改：

跳跳的两个手臂举着的有些违和感了，感觉是从帽子里面钻出来一样

系统收到后，只针对这一小段瑕疵重新生成，再自动剪回原片，其他已经满意的镜头纹丝不动。看下面「修改前」和「修改后」的对比图，修完之后整个动作瞬间顺眼多了。

四、实测踩出来的独家避坑 TIP：短手萌宠千万别写这个动作

跑完这一整套片子，我顺手总结了一条特别值钱的实测经验，能直接帮你少踩一大半穿模雷区：

3D 萌宠角色天生头大、手臂短，在写分镜动作或改图提示词时，尽量不要让它们做「双手高举过头顶」的动作！

只要你让短手小动物硬把东西高举过头顶，AI 模型为了强行满足指令，极容易触发下面这 3 种高频翻车：

1、手臂直接从帽子里钻出来，看着极其诡异。

2、小短胳膊被强行拉长，破坏原本圆润可爱的三头身比例。

3、莫名其妙多长出一双爪子，一眼假。

**最稳的正确解法是什么？**直接改成让它们把物体 「顶在头上托着」（比如让小云朵乖乖趴在跳跳的草帽顶上，小兔子双手自然扬起辅助托着），既符合短手萌宠的物理比例，萌感还直接翻倍！

五、完整 6 步实操演示 + 留一个下期王炸彩蛋

如果你更习惯跟着视频操作，我把上面 6 步完整流程和避坑对比浓缩成了一段 1 分 40 秒的实操讲解视频，每一步点哪个按钮都在画面里圈出来了，直接照着点就行：

看到这里，眼尖的朋友估计已经发现了什么不对劲的地方——

上面这段 1 分 40 秒里，在书房镜头前娓娓道来、口型自然、手势流畅的「小禾老师」，其实根本不是真人实拍！

她是我用下面 这一张静态人像图 + 一段声音，直接通过 Renoise AI 的数字人生成功能 跑出来的知识讲解主播：

现在你再回头看开头 对标账号 02 的变现套路，是不是瞬间通透了？

以前做矩阵号，拍萌宠动画要一套工具，自己不敢露脸又想做「AI 教程 / 干货口播 / 知识付费」又要折腾另一套设备、化妆打光背台词。现在同一个工具里，一边用 3D 萌宠动画 Skill 稳定日更吸泛流量，一边拿一张照片用数字人skill 功能批量出教程口播承接会员与变现，一个人就能跑出小团队的产能。

这篇篇幅已经很长了，关于怎么只用「一张图 + 一个声音」零出镜做出这种口型自然、能讲课能带货的知识讲解数字人，我留到下期单独写一篇保姆级拆解，想蹲的朋友先点个关注防走丢！

六、工具实测体验与黑五限时省钱窗口

实测跑完这一整轮，Renoise AI 最省心的地方在于把「写分镜、锁角色、出有声成片、局部精修」全打包进了现成的 Skill 里，除了这次演示的 3D 萌宠动画，里面还自带数字人、口播、二次元番剧等一堆可直接复用的工作流，特别适合一个人低成本测赛道、稳定跑日更。
